captions.detailed: A clamp-on task lamp styled for desk-edge mounting. It features a dark-colored, C-shaped clamp with a screw mechanism at the base, from which a dual-link spring-balanced arm extends. The arm consists of thin silver parallel rods connected by dark hinge blocks, complete with visible tension springs running along the center. At the end of the second arm link, a simple cylindrical black lamp shade is attached via a tilting hinge, housing a light source inside.
captions.instruction: Generate a desk-edge clamp-on task lamp as an articulated model. It should include a C-shaped desk clamp with a tightening screw, a lower arm link, an upper arm link, and a cylindrical lamp shade. Connect the parts with revolute joints: one at the clamp base for arm rotation, one at the elbow joint between the two arms, and one at the lamp head for tilting the shade. Use dark-colored materials for the clamp, hinges, and shade, and metallic silver for the parallel arm rods and balancing springs.
captions.factory: Construct the lamp hierarchically using an ArticulatedObject. First, build the clamp base using a combination of vertical and horizontal boxes to form the C-clamp, and cylinders for the tightening screw. Second, create the lower arm link by combining parallel cylindrical rods, a central helical spring (using a lofted or swept spiral path), and blocky end joints. Third, duplicate or construct a similar upper arm link. Fourth, model the lamp head as a hollow cylinder with an internal emission disk. Finally, link these parts sequentially using revolute joints at the base, elbow, and head, specifying their rotation axes and motion limits.
